submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on the token that fixes the frame of a new clause or text: the first token when it alone sets the frame (a pronoun subject, subordinator, discourse marker, or imperative verb), or, after a generic 'The X' opening, the subject noun, copula or auxiliary, or disambiguating completion (a unit noun such as 'light', the period of 'a.m.', a frame-completing adjunct head such as 'at') that establishes what the sentence is about. The same token is silent when it does not resolve an opening frame ('was' after 'day', 'light' without the quantity context, a pronoun mid-paragraph), and downstream continuations never change the peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Martinez boarded the night train in Denver with two suitcases and a paper map. Elena followed behind him carrying coffee, tickets, blankets, apples, notebooks, pencils. Priya claimed the window seat across the aisle and sketched bridges, tunnels, rivers. Tomas unpacked sandwiches, oranges, cheese, crackers, chocolate, pickles, napkins, cups. Ruth photographed signal towers, freight yards, crossings, depots, water tanks, silos. Denver faded behind tinted glass while dispatchers waved lanterns beside freezing rails. Omaha brought thunder, rain, hail, wind, gusts across darkened platforms. Slowly the coaches rattled past stockyards, grain elevators, refineries, lumber mills, quarries. Quietly conductors punched tickets, checked berths, closed curtains, dimmed corridors, locked cabinets. Carson narrated stories about miners, engineers, surveyors, conductors, porters, cooks, clerks. Elena peeled oranges, shared segments, saved rinds, traded napkins, refilled cups, hummed tunes. Tomas shuffled cards, dealt hands, collected chips, tallied scores, laughed loudly, lost gracefully. Ruth developed photographs in the cramped washroom using trays, timers, tongs, chemicals, clips. Priya annotated timetables, circled junctions, underlined connections, starred towns, dated margins, doodled borders. Chicago approached through fog, smoke, drizzle, sirens, scaffolding, cranes, crowds, neon. Carefully porters unloaded trunks, crates, bicycles, skis, instruments, parcels, cages, strollers. Reno greeted travelers with trumpets, banners, crowds, confetti, cameras, cheers, handshakes, songs. Martinez bought postcards, stamps, jerky, peanuts, magazines, batteries, socks, string, tape. Elena mailed letters, postcards, sketches, poems, receipts, coupons, maps, clippings, notes. Near midnight cooks served soup, bread, stew, pie, cocoa, potatoes, beans, rice, pudding. Beyond Omaha dispatchers rerouted freight, cleared sidings, flagged crossings, fueled engines, swapped crews. Sleeping passengers snored softly beneath wool blankets while wheels clicked over joints. Reading lamps buzzed faintly above green seats as children swapped comics, stickers, cards. Drawing pads slid across tables whenever brakes squealed near mountain curves. Nevada desert stretched wide outside frosted windows across salt flats, dunes, ridges. Sierra peaks towered northward above pine forests, frozen lakes, granite walls, passes. Tomas traded seats with Ruth to photograph sunrise over distant mesas. Priya brewed tea in a dented kettle and poured cups for neighbors nearby. Elena mended a torn strap using needles, thread, patches, glue, pins, tape. Quietly snow began falling past wires, poles, fences, barns, silos, tanks. Carson Valley welcomed dawn with church bells, barking dogs, roosters, tractors, smoke. Martinez counted mileposts, tunnels, trestles, signals, crossings, sidings, sheds, tanks. Martinez flipped on the small reading light beside the sleeper door and waited for Elena to return from the dining car.
